report.executive_summary: WO-03 screens four compute node packages for one fixed data-center workload on a single declared common test basis. All four candidates pass both policy gates (quality at least 80, raw defects at most 5), so the ranking rests entirely on measured energy per acceptance batch. Measured values: P3 10 Wh, P2 22 Wh, P1 28 Wh, P4 49 Wh. P3 leads by 12 Wh over P2, 18 Wh over P1 and 39 Wh over P4, cuts of 55, 64 and 80 percent. I recommend P3, the lowest-energy qualifying package (quality 97, four defects). No supplied field can close the 39 Wh gap to P4. Cost, delivery, maintenance and field reliability remain unverified and are logged as open questions.
report.figure_caption: WO-03 illustration: gates pass all four; measured Wh per batch on a 0-50 Wh axis, gaps 12/18/39 Wh to leader P3 (recommended); axis limits stated per the prior handover for checkable proportions.

recommendation.rationale: P3 is the lowest-energy qualifying package: 10 Wh against 22, 28 and 49 Wh, with quality 97 and four defects inside the ceiling. All four qualify, so the energy rule decides, and the 39 Wh margin over P4 cannot be closed by any supplied field. Unverified cost, delivery, maintenance and reliability stay out of the ranking and are logged as open questions.

sections.body: Both gates are binary. Quality: P4 98, P3 97, P2 95, P1 87 - every package clears the 80 floor; P1 clears it by only 7 points. Defects: P1 0, P2 0, P4 2, P3 4 - all within the ceiling of 5, so nothing is screened out and energy alone decides. Ascending by measured energy: P3 10, P2 22, P1 28, P4 49 Wh. Gaps to the leader are +12, +18 and +39 Wh. There is no quality-energy trade-off: the leader holds the second-highest quality, while the highest-quality package P4 is the most energy-expensive.
sections.heading: Package gates: eligibility and ranking

sections.body: After the gates, energy is the only measured discriminator. The P4-P3 margin is 39 Wh, 4.9 times the leader's reading; no realistic repeat-run noise on a fixed acceptance batch approaches that scale, so the ordering is robust. Quality differences among P2, P3 and P4 are 1-3 index points and change no gate outcome; P1 at 87 sits 10 points below P4 but remains comfortably qualified. Defect counts 0/0/4/2 are all permissible and counted raw, so P3's four defects carry no severity weighting. A tightened quality gate of 95 would remove only P1 and leave the ranking unchanged.
sections.heading: 4-way energy comparison and sensitivity

sections.body: The trusted table records only quality, raw defects and measured energy. Cost, delivery, maintenance and field reliability are unverified and stay outside the ranking; no preference can be imported without source data. This matters most for P4: its 39 Wh premium is exactly the size of margin that unverified reliability claims are usually invoked to justify, and none is on file, so none is credited. For P1 and P2 the gap runs the other way: quality 87 and 95 with zero defects may reflect shallow inspection rather than genuine cleanliness. Repeat-run variance behind the 10 Wh reading remains the only measured-data question.
sections.heading: Field gaps in the supplied evidence

sections.body: Six questions define the verification pass. 1 Justify the 10 Wh reading against repeat-run variance; none was supplied. 2 Verify defect arithmetic: counts 0/0/4/2 sit under the ceiling, but severity is unrecorded. 3 Measure whether recalibrating the declared common test basis could shift relative energies. 4 Where candidate four's 39 Wh deficit could be repaid: only unverified reliability or cost data; none exists. 5 Zero-defect P1 and P2 differ from the leader on energy alone, not quality. 6 Lastly, confirm that no unverified field entered the ranking. Answering these six items closes the WO-03 evidence record.
